purpose: Canonical temporal qualification cases distinguishing RTMPS session failures from general WAN outages, brief ACK stalls, runtime replacement, and evidence gaps

active_episode_matrix.scope: Detect, persist, and restart when a confirmed ACK-stall episode crosses its candidate correlation deadline, passes through missing or ineligible source evidence, and recovers through FFmpeg replacement in the same runtime

cases.description: Reconstruct without secrets a history in which general WAN stays UP, ACKs for the old target stall, and a new FFmpeg generation restores ACKs within the same Pod/container/runtime

Reconstruct without secrets a history where general WAN and ACK progress were healthy until RTMPS EOF invalidated the source generation temporarily, followed by FFmpeg-only replacement in the same Pod/container/runtime
Do not promote a one-interval ACK stall to an episode; discard the candidate when ACKs resume for the same target
Create a durable recovered episode only when an ACK stall with send pressure is immediately followed by FFmpeg replacement in the same runtime
Record same-session recovery when ACKs resume for the same target after the confirmation interval
Do not carry an old candidate into a new RTMPS episode when the Pod, container, or runtime generation changes
Do not promote a temporary source failure to session loss when the same FFmpeg identity returns
Do not link to the old FFmpeg if the Pod, container, or runtime generation changes after source failure
Do not link FFmpeg replacement more than 45 seconds after source failure to the same session-loss episode
Missing, arbitrary invalid, stale, or future observations alone cannot start an FFmpeg session-loss candidate
Do not classify rate-ineligible samples during in-flight effects or production behavior changes as spontaneous session loss
A late episode cannot justify transport gaps before its started_at
A late episode cannot justify owner UNKNOWN before its started_at
ACK=0 for the old target appears first; a late signed session-loss episode then confirms its replacement by the new target
Bind one episode when platform DOWN arrives first, followed by an ACTIVE RTMPS episode for the same origin target and a RECOVERED packet with the successor target
Without a matching signed replacement episode, treat ACK regression on the same target as insufficient evidence and pause certification instead of declaring SUT FAIL
An episode with a source start time after a late ACK regression cannot resolve that regression, even if its replay visibility time is newer
Late ACKs for an old target update only its own high-water mark and never revert the active target after a successor is confirmed
Bind saved gates to the terminal sample hash of the committed byte prefix, epoch, and config, not only sample count; reject a different prefix hash
Limit target history to 128 identities; after the limit, pause formal certification rather than adopting a new active target
